title: Space and its effect on you
html:
This morning I had a great chat to Lauren on Skype. She is in Prague right now and we are into week four of her three month trip. We discussed her trip and our goals for when she comes home.

What I have noticed is that it is the space that is making these conversations better and our goals clearer. Travel has been a big part of her plans for a long time, so it has taken up a lot of real estate in her mind, whereas mine is mostly taken up with Spikemail and ideas for Spikemail clients. So now we have got the space, and time, to think about things, we have got very clear about what we want.

I am not suggesting you go on an OE, like Lauren is, to get some space - but I do recommend you find some space to think. I have written about this before and usually suggest that just getting 10 minutes here and there will work. However, watching my friends and colleagues struggle with time issues and commitments with children and the like, I realise that this isn’t as easy as I originally thought.

So, what to do? I don’t know what will work for you. I could write a big list of things that might help but, in the end, it comes down to you. You need space to think clearly. This could be an uncluttered home, getting to work 30 minutes earlier or even staying later. Think about it though, and strive to find some space.
